title: Electrochemical CO2 capture by quinone-functionalized ruthenium polypyridine complexes

compounds.name: [Ru(bpy)2(phendione)]2+
compounds.quote: specifically [Ru(bpy)2(phendione)]2+ and [Ru (bpy)2(NQphen)]2+ (where phendione is 1,10-phenanthroline-5,6-dione; NQphen is benzo[i]dipyrido[3,2-a:2′,3′- c]phenazine-10,15-dione, and bpy is 2,2′-bipyridine)

compounds.name: [Ru(bpy)2(NQphen)]2+
compounds.quote: specifically [Ru(bpy)2(phendione)]2+ and [Ru (bpy)2(NQphen)]2+ (where phendione is 1,10-phenanthroline-5,6-dione; NQphen is benzo[i]dipyrido[3,2-a:2′,3′- c]phenazine-10,15-dione, and bpy is 2,2′-bipyridine)

compounds.name: NQphen
compounds.quote: the NQphen ligand alone exhibited a significantly lower log(K) of 2.1

conditions.quote: DMSO was used as the solvent with tetrabutylammonium hexafluorophosphate [NBu4][PF6] (0.1 M) as the supporting electrolyte.
The system was sequentially saturated with nitrogen, 20 % CO2, and 100 % CO2, with a saturation time of 10 min for each condition.

measurements.quote: the first, a quasi-reversible wave at −0.17 V vs Ag/AgCl, was assigned to the formation of the monoradical species (Q/Q•−)
the second quasi-reversible wave at −0.81 V vs Ag/AgCl corresponded to the conversion of the radical into the oxyanion (Q•−/Q2−)
the first reduction of the NQphen ligand, corresponding to the formation of the radical ion (Q/Q•-), exhibited a half-wave potential at −0.46 V vs Ag/ AgCl
the second reduction, leading to the formation of the oxy­anion (Q•/Q2−), occurred at −0.97 V vs Ag/AgCl
yielding values of 5.8 for [Ru(bpy)2(phendione)]2+ and 7.2 for [Ru(bpy)2(NQphen)]2+

the NQphen ligand alone exhibited a significantly lower log(K) of 2.1

observations.quote: suggesting the reversible formation of adducts, similar to carbonates, between the oxygen anion of the reduced quinone and the electrophilic carbon of CO2.
